Nema vs Atlassian Rovo

Choose cross-team Slack work or Atlassian-centered agents.

Rovo brings search, chat, and agents to Jira, Confluence, and connected knowledge. Nema gives every Slack channel a focused coworker.

The short answer

Atlassian Rovo combines enterprise search, chat, and configurable agents with Jira, Confluence, Jira Service Management, and connected sources. Rovo also has an official Slack app with direct messages, mentions, channel triggers, thread summaries, and access to agents. Nema starts with Slack rather than Atlassian. Each channel has a coworker configured for that team's context and tools.

Choose Rovo when Jira and Confluence are the core work system. Choose Nema when several functions coordinate through Slack and the channel is where the agent works and asks for approval.

Checked September 22, 2026. Atlassian's guide to the Rovo Slack app documents current direct messages, mentions, sidebar context, bot permissions, and triggers. Its agent guide covers agent setup and skills.

A sprint planning packet

An engineering channel needs to prepare for sprint planning. The inputs include the approved backlog, issue dependencies, recent channel decisions, and readiness criteria. The result should identify unready work and unresolved capacity questions.

With Nema, the engineering channel teaches its coworker the readiness rules and approved sources. Nema posts a planning packet in the thread, cites the evidence behind each exception, and proposes follow-ups. The engineering lead reviews any intended issue changes before they happen. Corrections remain with that channel's guidance.

Rovo can perform the same job close to Jira and Confluence. Its agents can use Atlassian knowledge and perform specialized skills such as creating or editing Jira work items with permission. In Slack, people can DM Rovo, mention it in channels, summarize threads, or configure keyword and emoji triggers for Rovo or a custom agent.

Choose Nema when

Choose Nema when the work crosses functions and Slack is the common operating layer. A project channel can combine discussion with authorized sources from several systems and use one visible approval path. Teams can also choose models and configure each channel differently.

This fit is useful when Jira and Confluence are important sources but do not define the whole workflow. Verify the exact Atlassian connection and action before relying on it.

Choose Rovo when

Choose Rovo when Jira, Confluence, and Jira Service Management contain the authoritative work. Rovo's native access and Atlassian permission model reduce the need to reconstruct that context elsewhere. Search, Chat, and Agents form one system for Atlassian-heavy teams.

Rovo's Slack app does more than notify. Channel triggers can respond to messages, keywords, or emoji, and the private sidebar can use the open channel as context. Both products can participate in Slack channels.

Check bot permissions

Rovo's channel setup uses a managed Atlassian bot account. Atlassian warns administrators to grant that bot only information safe for people in the channel because public-channel responses use bot permissions. Private DMs use the user's permissions. That distinction deserves a real access test.

For Nema, test the requester's connected access and channel policy. In both products, try the task as two users with different source permissions and inspect who authors a proposed issue change.

Common questions

Can Rovo work inside Slack?

Yes. Rovo supports direct messages, mentions, sidebar chat, thread summaries, and configured channel triggers. It can also expose custom Rovo agents in Slack.

Does Rovo only use Atlassian data?

No. Rovo supports connectors to third-party sources, including Slack. Its deepest native fit remains Jira, Confluence, and other Atlassian products.

Which is better for Jira work?

Rovo has the stronger native fit for Jira search and actions. Nema may fit when Jira work is one part of a broader Slack-led process that also involves other teams and systems.
